mcat_description.short: A Control Panel Cabin is a prefabricated, skid-mounted or modular steel structure designed to house industrial electrical control panels — such as MCC, APFC, PLC, VFD, and SCADA panels — at industrial sites, substations, and infrastructure projects. Sold as a complete custom-built unit, typically fabricated from mild steel or GI sheet with insulation, ventilation, and electrical fittings.
mcat_description.long: Control Panel Cabins are prefabricated walk-in or skid-mounted enclosure structures built to protect and house electrical control equipment including Motor Control Centres (MCC), APFC panels, PLC/SCADA systems, VFD panels, and distribution boards in outdoor or semi-outdoor industrial environments. Constructed primarily from mild steel (MS) or galvanised iron (GI) sheet with options for PUF insulation, false ceiling, anti-skid flooring, and integrated ventilation or air conditioning, these cabins are custom-fabricated to buyer-specified dimensions and electrical load requirements. They are widely deployed at power substations, water treatment plants, manufacturing facilities, oil & gas installations, solar power plants, and infrastructure project sites where permanent building construction is impractical. In the Indian market, these structures are sold per piece as turnkey prefabricated units, with customisation covering size, material grade, IP protection level, insulation type, and internal electrical fittings.

market_context: Control Panel Cabins in India are prefabricated steel structures (distinct from panel enclosures/cabinets) used to house electrical control equipment at industrial and infrastructure sites. The dominant construction material is mild steel (MS) sheet, with GI sheet and PUF sandwich panel variants for insulated or weatherproof applications. Key differentiators in the Indian market include insulation type (PUF vs. non-insulated), air conditioning provision, IP/weatherproofing level, and internal electrical fittings. APFC panel cabins represent a well-recognised sub-type in India, driven by electricity board power factor penalty regulations that make APFC installations mandatory for large industrial consumers. MCC panel cabins are the other dominant sub-type, widely used in manufacturing and infrastructure projects. The Indian market is served by a fragmented base of fabricators and portable cabin manufacturers concentrated in Gujarat (Ahmedabad, Mahesana), Maharashtra (Nagpur, Thane), and Karnataka (Bellary). Buyers are predominantly EPC contractors, plant owners, and government infrastructure agencies who procure on a project basis. The product sits at the intersection of the prefabricated structures industry and the electrical panel industry — sellers may be either cabin fabricators or electrical panel manufacturers who add cabin fabrication capability. A critical naming distinction: 'Control Panel Cabin' (this MCAT — a prefabricated room/structure) must not be confused with 'Control Panel Enclosure' or 'Control Panel Cabinet' (a sheet-metal box that houses panel components — a separate product category).
